evidence: src/domain/Order.ts: class Order enforces its invariants in the constructor and in advanceTo and cancel, always throwing DomainError and typing status as OrderStatus.
src/domain/Product.ts: class Product keeps the stock rules in reserve and release, which share the private helper assertValidQuantity; it throws DomainError.
src/domain/OrderRepository.ts: interface OrderRepository has findById, save and listByStatus(status?: OrderStatus), working only with Order.
src/domain/ProductRepository.ts: interface ProductRepository has findById, save and list, working only with Product.
src/domain/OrderStatus.ts: OrderStatus is derived from orderStatuses and used by both Order and OrderRepository.
src/domain/DomainError.ts: the single error type used by both entities.

Minor overlap: Order's constructor checks Number.isInteger(line.quantity) || line.quantity <= 0, similar to Product.assertValidQuantity. It guards a different input, so it is not counted as a violation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the order-and-catalogue domain. Order.ts and Product.ts are the entities. OrderRepository.ts and ProductRepository.ts are interfaces for storing them, each working only with its own entity. OrderStatus.ts defines the set of status values, and DomainError.ts is the one error type. The module's abstractions are used consistently: every invariant failure throws DomainError, and status is always typed as OrderStatus, derived from orderStatuses. Order status changes and cancellation rules live only in Order (advanceTo, cancel). Stock rules live only in Product (reserve, release, assertValidQuantity). Two small overlaps exist. First, Order's constructor repeats the positive-integer quantity check that Product.assertValidQuantity also makes. Second, the nextByStatus map in Order.advanceTo lists the statuses in the same order as orderStatuses. The quantity check is a one-line check on two different inputs (an order line and a stock reservation). The status map is typed Record<OrderStatus, …>, so the compiler forces it to cover every status. Neither is a meaningful duplicated rule, a split into unrelated concerns, or a bypass of the module's abstractions.
